technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The useful quality of a commodity, one of the two opposed sides of its nature.
A commodity's power to be exchanged, expressed in the quantity of another commodity or of money it gets.
The socially fixed quantity of human labour embodied in a commodity, shown in its price.
The form a commodity's value takes when it is expressed as money.
The change of form a commodity goes through in exchange, as in C–M–C.
The chain of sales and purchases that links commodity owners, which differs from barter.
variants_seen: circulation of the products of social labour

technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The one commodity, gold as money, in which the value of all other commodities is socially expressed.
The average labour time needed to make a commodity under normal conditions, which sets its value.
Labour counted only as expended human labour, apart from its concrete form.
Money used only as the means by which commodities change hands.
The continual movement of money from one owner to the next, a course rather than a circuit.
How many times a given coin changes hands in a given time.
variants_seen: velocity of the currency of money

technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: Money withdrawn from circulation and kept in its money-form.
Money used to settle debts that fall due after the sale has happened.
Money used only as a measure in calculation, not as cash in hand.
Money on the world market, where it appears as bullion and is no longer only a local token.
The point where the split between sale and purchase becomes an open break and money is demanded as hard cash.
Value that grows by circulating, the form of money that expands itself.
The increment by which the sum advanced in M–C–M grows, defined as the excess over the original value.
Value that expands by moving through its forms of money and commodities.
Selling in order to buy (C–M–C), which begins with a sale and ends with a purchase.
The normal form of exchange, in which commodities of equal value are swapped.
The mental and physical capacity a person uses when producing; sold to the buyer as a commodity.
Set by the value of the means of subsistence needed to maintain and reproduce the worker.
The goods a worker needs to live and reproduce, which fix the value of labour-power.
A movement that returns to its starting form, as commodity to commodity or money to money.

voice_attribution_risks.note: Condillac's long quoted passage opens with 'It is not true'; a reader may miss that Marx rejects it.
Torrens's 'Effectual demand' is quoted in the body text; Marx's answer follows, so keep the quote and the rebuttal clearly split.
Two propositions, 'Capital is money' and 'Capital is commodities', come from Mercantilist and Mill sources, then Marx says value is the active factor.
'inwardly circumcised Jews' is Marx's satirical image of the capitalist's view of commodities; the wording is a sharp, antisemitic-tinged image that a rewriter must handle deliberately.
The 'Eden of the innate rights of man' passage is ironic; a reader could take Freedom/Equality/Property/Bentham as Marx's approval.
Storch's 'risks nothing' and the bakers' report are quoted inside footnotes; keep the attribution clear.
Adam Smith's quoted passage on the money quantity is partly praised, partly rejected by Marx; a reader may take it as Marx's own view.
MacCulloch is praised for an 'anticipation' in the footnote; Marx's irony sits inside the quote; keep the mockery visible.

irony_examples.note: 'like a man of the good old stamp' mocks the weaver's innocent exchange.
'Although people do not look a gift-horse in the mouth, our friend does not frequent the market for the purpose of making presents.'
'our Hotspur' and the Bible seller who sells 'the water of everlasting life' for brandy.
'ce n'est que le premier pas qui coûte' jokes about the first step of paper money.
'He acts in earnest up to the Gospel of abstention' mocks the hoarder's virtues.
'the miser is merely a capitalist gone mad; the capitalist is a rational miser' is ironic about greed.
Pinto and MacCulloch are mocked for turning the trader into a moralist.
Torrens's 'power and inclination (!)' carries an exclamation mark as irony.
'Eden of the innate rights of man' ironically calls the market sphere a paradise.
the labourer 'bringing his own hide to market ... nothing to expect but a hiding' is grim comic irony.
